question: persister
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Astronomical transient surveys → alert-triggered single-cell follow-up
ideas.description: Borrowing from sky-survey alert brokers that trigger rapid follow-up on rare transients, continuously image millions of drug-treated cells, automatically flag the rare cells still dividing or re-entering cycle, then photoconvert/photo-tag only those cells and isolate them immediately for scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and proteomics. This profiles the actual survivors at the moment of divergence instead of averaging them away in bulk or in post-hoc resistant lines.

ideas.title: Control engineering Bode plots → drug delivered as a frequency sweep
ideas.description: As in system identification, drive the system with oscillating inputs across many frequencies: use microfluidics to deliver the targeted inhibitor as sinusoidal concentration waveforms with periods from minutes to days while recording pathway-activity reporters. Test whether pre-persister cells are defined by a distinct transfer function (slower, more damped signaling response) rather than by a static difference in baseline expression.

ideas.title: Metallurgical fatigue testing → extreme-value statistics of survival
ideas.description: Materials scientists separate pre-existing-flaw failure from accumulated-damage failure using single-overload versus cyclic loading and Weibull/extreme-value fits. Deliver matched total drug exposure as one continuous dose versus many intermittent pulses across thousands of replicate wells, then fit the survivor-fraction distributions to ask whether survival follows a weakest-link model (rare pre-existing states) or a damage-accumulation model (tolerance built during treatment).

ideas.title: Dendrochronology / isotope geochemistry → reading each survivor's recorded history
ideas.description: Like tree rings or ice cores storing a dated chemical record, apply sequential metabolic time-stamps before and during treatment (distinguishable 4sU/5-EU RNA pulses plus SILAC heavy-amino-acid pulses) so every cell carries layered, time-ordered evidence of its transcription and translation rates. Read these layers out in single surviving cells to reconstruct whether they were already slow-cycling or translationally quiet long before the drug was added.

ideas.title: Dynamical systems "critical slowing down" → early-warning signals of fate commitment
ideas.description: Ecosystems and climate systems show rising variance, autocorrelation, and recovery time before a regime shift. Record long high-frequency single-cell reporter traces through treatment and compute rolling variance, lag-1 autocorrelation, and relaxation time after small optogenetic or washout perturbations, testing whether future persisters display these slowing-down signatures hours before they visibly diverge from dying neighbors.
